quizName: Hardest Questions in Mississippi Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that cover your ankles provide the best protection. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not remove alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen by them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen by them.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What should proper motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever you find comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover both your arms and legs completely for proper protection.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about how it works, its features, and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend wants to ride their motorcycle after drinking?

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Get other friends to talk them out of it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of it.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do whatever you can to stop them. Asking multiple friends to pressure them not to ride is an effective approach.

questions.question: Why are turn signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They don't matter much because motorcycles are small.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
You should skip them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are harder to use than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use turn signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do. Use them when changing lanes or turning, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: If your turn seems obvious, should you use a turn signal?

options.text: No, a signal is not needed.
Only if you are at a red light.

questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if your plan seems obvious. Use signals every time, even if you don't see other drivers. There may be vehicles nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: What features should boots or shoes have for motorcycle riding?

options.text: Coverage of the ankle with support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Coverage of the ankle with support.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or heavy shoes tall enough to cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they won't catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Compare the height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine even if it is under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle you have not used before, what should you do?

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before you ride.
Ride normally, since all motorcycles are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before you ride.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before you ride, get familiar with the bike. Practice the gear pattern and test the throttle, clutch, and brakes.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider be more visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors and reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Always use your headlight and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: What is an advantage of wearing a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It does not block your side vision.
It can greatly reduce the severity of head injuries.
It makes it easier to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can greatly reduce the severity of head injuries.
questions.explanation: A helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot reach the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly when your feet can reach the ground while you are sitting on it. You should be able to reach and use the controls easily.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to check when choosing a helmet?

options.text: It meets Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: It meets Department of Transportation standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Blend in with traffic so other drivers do not notice you.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: Help other drivers see you by using your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles, look 12 seconds ahead, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Stay on the shoulder and out of traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: You should not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
You should not wear them because they make the controls harder to use.
You should only wear them on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or other durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and help protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: Which surface provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Several surfaces provide poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are more hazardous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Wet surfaces make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which surface is slippery?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. A small problem on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best grip?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers are more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: The best way to learn about your motorcycle is to read:

options.text: Ask someone with a different motorcycle.
Watch a television show about riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before your first ride. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride, you should:

options.text: Tell them to take quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have drunk too much. Do what you can to stop them, including taking their keys. Help them find another way home.
